summary: This room's five targets are not thin — they're saturated. Every single hop1 neighbor for all five (The Aftermath Frame, Tool Builder, Zoom Out to the Structure, assume multi-agent, The Remembering Page) already links back to its target, most as symmetric connects-to. The "reached_by 4-6" numbers are misleading: these pages are tightly wired into their own immediate BLUELINE or palace-development clusters, they just haven't been discovered yet by entries one ring further out. The genuine new wiring came from two different places: hop2 neighbors that share the target's own cited mechanism (ControlNet as Topology shares the exact depth/pose-plate → ControlNet → ink pipeline The Aftermath Frame's body already describes), and a straight read of each target's own body prose turning up entries it names but never linked — the unsung-path scan did more work here than the formal walk. assume multi-agent stayed genuinely null: its hop2 (ComfyUI, LoRA Trainer, BBS Blackboard, Concierge, Hero and Avatar Maker) share GPU/coordination proximity but none of their own bodies make the multi-tenant-safety claim specific to this entry — forcing it would have been the "had to force it" failure mode the brief warns against, so it's left alone.

typed_relations.label: armature-for-the-swing
typed_relations.rationale: The Aftermath Frame's own render pipeline is 'the depth / OpenPose plates → ControlNet / img2img → pen-flow ink' — that is exactly ControlNet as Topology's 'armature' (a depth map, a pose, an edge map is exactly that skeleton). Both already share Blocked, Not Prompted, Steer the Generator, and The Flow Field is the Spine as neighbors, but neither links directly to the other — this closes a real gap, not a proximity coincidence.
typed_relations.evidence: Aftermath Frame: 'the physical consequences + the depth / OpenPose plates → ControlNet / img2img → pen-flow ink'. ControlNet as Topology: 'A depth map, a pose, an edge map is exactly that skeleton; the render is the clay wrapped onto it.'

typed_relations.label: structure-from-scars
typed_relations.rationale: Zoom Out to the Structure's own worked examples ('a one-file RunPod pod-naming fix → The Commons', 'the toolbox convention') are literally tool-building scars becoming general discipline — exactly Tool Builder's subject. Tool Builder is the domain-specific elaboration (palace tooling) of the general zoom-out habit; Zoom Out is the ground.
typed_relations.evidence: Zoom Out: 'A one-file RunPod pod-naming fix → The Commons, a whole coordination layer for any shared external service.' Tool Builder: 'The discipline of building a tool that survives contact with a live, multi-agent palace... Each rule below is the compressed form of a real scar.'

typed_relations.label: checklist-growth
typed_relations.rationale: Tool Builder's own body names the mechanism by which its checklist grows and has no frontmatter link for it — an unsung path that also happens to be the inbound Tool Builder's assigned hop1/hop2 walk failed to surface (both rings were already saturated with existing links).
typed_relations.evidence: 'the deepest disciplines earn their own entries and link back with member-of... added by [[Harvest Ceremony|Harvest]], not by dumping every operational note at once.'

typed_relations.label: loads-the-memory
typed_relations.rationale: The Remembering Page's mechanism section states outright that Palace Enchantment is what loads its memory back in on waking — a precondition relation, named in body, absent from frontmatter and from the target's own hop1/hop2 list.
typed_relations.evidence: 'When the page is next cast, the memory loads alongside its body, so it wakes already carrying its past ([[Palace Enchantment]] loads it).'

typed_relations.label: debate-mode
typed_relations.rationale: Named as one of the two modes that shape what a page's memory forms — the sharpening counterpart to the Walk. Body-only citation.
typed_relations.evidence: 'A debate (a [[Dialectic]]) sharpens a contrary: two pages defend their grips and leave more distinct than they arrived.'

typed_relations.label: lifetime-closing
typed_relations.rationale: The entry explicitly names its own mechanism as the same pattern as Closing Well applied at a different scale — a session's end vs. a page's own life — which is exactly what 'mirrors' is for. Body-only citation.
typed_relations.evidence: 'And it is [[Closing Well]] across a page's own lifetime — each encounter ends by leaving an honest record so the next waking of this page can pick up where it left off.'
